disposition_reason: The original one-session retrieval/reconstruction task and corrected published retrieval score are recoverable. Native feature/reference parity, full reconstruction evaluation, exact historical preprocessing and sample manifests, a meaningful effect rule, and measured episode budgets remain unqualified; the feature-only component cannot admit an improvement win.

source_paper.title: MindEye2: Shared-Subject Models Enable fMRI-To-Image With 1 Hour of Data

evidence.locator: Sections 2, 3, 3.3; Table 1; Appendix A.2 and A.5 Table 8
evidence.supports: Original one-hour target, four-subject evaluation, shared-image test set, preprocessing and published endpoint panel.

evidence.locator: Retrieval metric correction; Usage; pretrained model configurations
evidence.supports: Corrected retrieval directions and scores; first-session adaptation of leave-target-subject-out checkpoints.
OpenCLIP token space, cosine top-1 retrieval, 30 draws of 300 paired samples and draw averaging.

evidence.locator: Parser --new_test; inference repeat handling and embedding/reconstruction production
evidence.supports: Source inference entrypoint and repeated-image handling must be preserved when producing evaluation features.

target.description: One-hour fMRI-to-image retrieval and reconstruction; primary ordered endpoint is corrected brain-query/image-candidate top-1 retrieval. Reconstruction remains a required companion panel, not an optional replacement endpoint.

dataset.description: Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD), full 40-session release used in the paper, with author MindEyeV2 derivatives. Exact paper-era neural, image, checkpoint and derivative file hashes are not yet authenticated.

cohort.description: Evaluate subjects 1, 2, 5 and 7; each target uses a shared model pretrained on the other seven NSD subjects. A single-subject or reduced-image result cannot substitute for this aggregate.

split.description: Adapt on the first scanning session, excluding shared1000 test images; retain the same 1,000 shared test images and their original repeat support for every training-duration condition. Do not replace this with the legacy prospective session-disjoint restriction.

inputs.description: Single-trial nsdgeneral fMRI responses and paired training images, seven-other-subject pretraining, and the source pretrained image-model resources. Match and record neural/image/checkpoint exposure; no test image identity or feature target may enter a candidate query.

preprocessing.description: GLMSingle normalized betas, 1.8-mm native-volume nsdgeneral voxels, voxel z-scoring from the full training partition before reducing to one session. The paper acknowledges this extra normalization exposure; a first-session-only normalization experiment is a separately labelled extension. Native repeat handling still requires parity verification.

metric.description: For each 300-item draw, flatten and L2-normalize paired OpenCLIP ViT-bigG-14/laion2b_s39b_b160k token embeddings; score the fraction whose true image has greatest cosine similarity to the brain query. Preserve corrected orientation and qualify native ties/RNG behavior.

aggregation.description: Average retrieval accuracy over 30 sampled 300-image pools per subject, then equally across the four paper subjects. Keep reverse retrieval and all reconstruction metrics separate. Repeated pools are Monte Carlo variation, not independent people.

comparison.primary_metric: Corrected one-hour image retrieval top-1 fraction (brain query, 300 image candidates)

published_baseline.description: 0.574 is the author-corrected one-hour Table 1 image retrieval mean (57.4%); corrected reverse retrieval is 0.790. This is a published result, not a local rerun or current-SOTA value.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: No authentic one-hour four-subject author-model rerun was executed. The pinned README supplies the pretrained checkpoint/adaptation route; its actual data, weights, preprocessing and complete metric parity remain to be qualified.

minimum_effect.rationale: A meaningful gain must exceed source rounding and measured rerun/Monte Carlo variability while preserving the declared reconstruction trade-off rule. No source-justified numeric margin or qualified rerun variance is available.

uncertainty.method: Predeclare a paired comparison across the four paper subjects with shared-image dependence and stochastic retrieval/reconstruction variability represented; choose the interval and decision rule before candidate evaluation.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Human participant; images are shared across participants and repeated retrieval pools are not independent biological replicates.
uncertainty.rationale: The notebook interval across 30 overlapping pools describes sampling variability and cannot establish a population-level improvement. Four source subjects limit inference.

paper_win_requires: Reproduce the corrected author baseline on the original four subjects, first-session adaptation, shared1000 population and source normalization exposure before comparing a candidate.

Exceed 0.574 on the original corrected image-retrieval endpoint by the predeclared meaningful effect and uncertainty rule; also exceed the qualified author rerun on identical inputs and retrieval pools.
Retain brain retrieval and the complete original reconstruction panel, with a predeclared joint/trade-off decision; a retrieval-only subset result is not success for the registered combined task.

Freeze candidate code, checkpoints, preprocessing, image-model resources and exposure ledger before final scoring; preserve original test identities. A new split, reduced cohort or altered normalization regime is an extension.

Document public test exposure and reproduce all source evaluation semantics, including repeated presentations and metric direction; the existing generated-control feature scorer is insufficient evidence.

current_sota.description: The source paper historical SOTA claim does not establish present SOTA. No current competing method comparison was verified.

episode.improvement_loop: After admission, iterate on the original training data and declared validation feedback within that training partition. Restore the full permitted first-session training allocation for final fitting and record all image/neural pretraining exposure. Do not tune from final shared1000 scores.
episode.candidate_freeze: Commit candidate algorithm, fitting/selection recipe, checkpoints, pretrained resources, exact trial/image manifests, native normalization/repeat rules and retrieval-pool schedule before final evaluation.
episode.final_evaluation: Run the frozen candidate and authentic author baseline on all four original subjects and the same shared1000 test images; report corrected retrieval and full reconstruction results, paired uncertainty and public-test exposure. Newly protected samples are a separate extension.
episode.baseline_policy: Published corrected score, reproduced author score and any separately verified current-SOTA score remain distinct. Local numerical controls or a weaker single-subject model cannot replace the source author baseline.

blocking_issues: Authenticate exact NSD/derivative/checkpoint manifests and source exposure, including normalization statistics from more than the adaptation session.
Reconcile legacy evaluator session-disjoint prospective protection with the original shared1000 test population; do not silently drop first-session test presentations.
Qualify native feature extraction, repeat aggregation, historical retrieval RNG/ties and all original reconstruction metrics; no authentic full-panel rerun exists.
Freeze source-task reconstruction trade-offs, meaningful effect and participant-aware uncertainty without treating 30 overlapping pools as independent samples.
Set concrete access/validation/final-query and compute budgets and protect final scoring; public source test exposure must be disclosed.

legacy.notes: The original task and initial-evaluator-v1 remain calibration materials. Frozen-pool feature scoring and generated tests do not establish native reproduction or stronger-than-paper performance; their prospective split/RNG policies must not redefine the paper task.
